facts.statement: Gobisaurus was a herbivorous basal ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Gobisaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China (Nei Mongol Zizhiqu).

facts.statement: The genus Gobisaurus is monotypic, containing only the single species Gobisaurus domoculus.
facts.quote: The genus is monotypic, containing only the species Gobisaurus domoculus.

facts.statement: A Sino-Soviet Expedition discovered the skeleton of Gobisaurus in the Gobi Desert of Inner Mongolia between 1959 and 1960.
facts.quote: The Sino-Soviet Expeditions (1959–1960) discovered an ankylosaurian skeleton in the Gobi Desert of Inner Mongolia near Moartu, in the region of the Alashan Desert.

facts.statement: Matthew K. Vickaryous, Anthony P. Russell, Philip John Currie, and Zhao Xijin named and described Gobisaurus domoculus in 2001.
facts.quote: In 2001, Matthew K. Vickaryous, Anthony P. Russell, Philip John Currie and Zhao Xijin named and described the type species Gobisaurus domoculus.

facts.statement: The generic name Gobisaurus means "Gobi (Desert) lizard," referring to where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name means "Gobi (Desert) lizard," referring to its provenance.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Gobisaurus domoculus at 6 meters and its weight at 3.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó su longitud corporal en 6 metros, su peso en 3,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: The eye sockets of Gobisaurus domoculus were 20% of the skull length, and the external nostrils were 23% of the skull length.
facts.quote: Las órbitas eran el 20 por ciento de la longitud craneal y los orificios nasales externos de un 23 por ciento.

facts.statement: Gobisaurus domoculus can be distinguished from its relative Shamosaurus scutatus by having a maxillary tooth row length of 26.6% of total skull length, compared to 40% in Shamosaurus.
facts.quote: Pero los dos taxones se pueden distinguir por diferencias en la longitud de la fila de dientes maxilar' 26,6% en lugar del 40% de la longitud total del cráneo en Gobisaurus

facts.statement: Gobisaurus domoculus shares cranial similarities with Shamosaurus scutatus, including elliptical orbital fenestrae, large rounded external nares, a trapezoidal dorsal profile with a narrow rostrum, quadratojugal protuberances, and caudolaterally directed paroccipital processes.
facts.quote: El G. domoculus comparte muchas semejanzas craneales con el S. scutatus, incluyendo ventanas orbitales elípticas rodeadas por el escamoso, grandes orificios nasales externos redondeados y un perfil dorsal trapezoidal con un rostro estrecho, protuberancias cuadratojugal, y procesos paroccipital caudolateralmente dirigidos.

facts.statement: Gobisaurus lived approximately 93 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 93 millones de años, en el Turoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Gobisaurus spans from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2014, Victoria Arbour concluded that Zhongyuansaurus might be a junior synonym of Gobisaurus based on the extensive postcranial remains found in its type specimen.
facts.quote: In 2014, Victoria Arbour concluded that Zhongyuansaurus, the type specimen of which, HGM 41HIII-0002, includes extensive postcranial remains, was a possible junior synonym of Gobisaurus.

facts.statement: Victoria Arbour denied the distinction regarding cranial sculpting between Gobisaurus and Shamosaurus, concluding the degree of sculpting was approximately the same.
facts.quote: Esta última diferencia fue negada por Arbor, quien concluyó que el grado de escultura era aproximadamente el mismo.

rejected.quote: The specific name means "hidden from view" in Latin, referring to its being overlooked for three decades.
